URBAN AFFAIRS · WORKING DRAFT

A city in motion:
the changing commute

By Jamie Laurent · October 7, 2026

At eight in the morning, the cycle lanes along the river are already busy. Commuters weave past delivery vans and early café customers, part of a shift that is reshaping how the city moves.

Cycling in the city increased by 24% between 2022 and 2025. The rise has become a central argument in the debate over how much street space should be given to bikes.

But the scale of that change depends on who is counting. Transport officials, independent researchers and local cycling groups each offer a different picture of the morning commute.

A longer road to change

The city began expanding its protected cycle network in 2018. Since then, new routes have connected residential neighbourhoods with the centre, though gaps remain at several busy junctions.

For residents, the discussion is about more than numbers. It is about the everyday experience of getting to work, taking children to school and moving safely through a changing city.
